Video Vocabulary: Disrupt, Stabilize & Friends

Silent clips · freeze-frame predictions · GIF match

Level 3 — Vocabulary

 

Seven Words for Change

These words describe a change or what a change leaves behind. A picture cannot show a change, so today we use short silent clips.

WordMeaningExample
disrupt (verb)stop something from going normallyA power cut disrupted our online class.
stabilize (verb)make something steady, stop it from shaking or changingThe doctors stabilized the patient.
thwart (verb)stop a plan from succeedingThe police thwarted the robbery.
knock-on effects (noun)the extra problems that one problem causes laterOne late train had knock-on effects all morning.
grounded (adjective)kept on the ground; not allowed to flyThick fog grounded every helicopter on the island.
chaotic (adjective)with no order and no controlThe first day of the sale was chaotic.
residual (adjective)small and left over after most of it has goneThe doctor said the residual pain would last one more week.
 

Word Families

Pattern: verb → noun → adjective. disrupt → disruption → disruptive
VerbNounAdjective
disruptdisruptiondisruptive
stabilizestabilitystable
thwart—thwarted
ground—grounded
—chaoschaotic
—residueresidual
—knock-on effectsknock-on
Past tense: the four verbs are all regular. Add -ed (or -d): disrupted, stabilized, thwarted, grounded. Chaotic, residual and knock-on are not verbs, so they never take -ed.
 

Activity 1 — Silent Clip 1 of 4: You Tell the Story

Watch each clip. No sound, no words. Say one sentence about what happened. Use one word or phrase from the box, in the past tense if it is a verb. Then click to compare.

Word box: disrupt · stabilize · thwart · knock-on effects · grounded · chaotic · residual
Watch the clip. No sound.

1. What happened? Say one sentence with a word from the box.

A dog disrupted the yoga class. — People were doing yoga. The dog ran through the class and they fell over, so the class could not go on normally.

 

Activity 1 — Silent Clip 2 of 4: You Tell the Story

Word box: disrupt · stabilize · thwart · knock-on effects · grounded · chaotic · residual
Watch the clip. No sound.

2. What happened? Say one sentence with a word from the box.

The waiter stabilized the tray. — It was tilting and the glasses were sliding. He put his other hand under it and held it steady.

 

Activity 1 — Silent Clip 3 of 4: You Tell the Story

Watch the clip. No sound.

3. What happened? Say one sentence with a word from the box.

Mixed Practice

Fill each gap with one word or phrase from the box. If the gap shows a verb, put it in the past tense. Answer first, then click to check.

Word box: disrupt · stabilize · thwart · knock-on effects · grounded · chaotic · residual

1. Heavy rain ___ (thwart) our plan to paint the fence.

thwarted — the plan did not succeed at all.

2. Because of the strike, the airline ___ (ground) forty flights.

grounded — the planes had to stay on the ground.

3. One broken traffic light caused ___ across the whole city.

knock-on effects — one small problem made many more problems later.

4. The fire was out, but we could still smell ___ smoke.

residual — a small amount was left after most of it had gone.

5. The market was so ___ that I could not hear my friend.

chaotic — there was no order and no control.

6. Loud building work ___ (disrupt) the exam yesterday.

disrupted — the exam could not run normally.

7. Steel cables ___ (stabilize) the new crane.

stabilized — the cables made it steady.

 

Summary

IdeaWordsRemember
Something stops or breaks downdisrupt · thwart · chaoticdisrupt = a process cannot go on normally; thwart = a plan does not succeed; chaotic = no order and no control
Something is held steady or held backstabilize · groundedstabilize = stop the shaking; grounded = kept on the ground, not allowed to fly
What is left, or what followsknock-on effects · residualknock-on effects = the later problems one problem causes; residual = the small part left over
Past tensethe four verbs are regularadd -ed / -d: disrupted, stabilized, thwarted, grounded
